source_text:
ἐπιστήσεις δὲ αὐτοὺς καὶ ἐκ τοῦ τὸν Χριστὸν εἶναι δικαιο ύνην. ἐν μὲν οὖν τῷ
εὐεργετικῷ ἐμφαίνεται ἡ ἀγαθωσύνη, ἐν δὲ τῷ κατ' ἀξίαν ἀπονεμη τικῷ ἡ
δικαιοσύνη, ἐν δὲ τῷ ἐπιστημονικῷ τοῦ τῶν ὅλων λόγου ἡ ἀλήθεια. [v 10]
δοκιμάζοντες τί ἐστὶν εὐάρεστον τῷ Κυρίῳ. χρεία τοῦ μετὰ βουλῆς πάντα ποιεῖν, ἵνα
περισκοποῦντες ἕκαστον τῶν πρακτέων ἀπὸ ἐξετάσεως τὰ μὲν δοκιμαστὰ καὶ
εὐάρεστα τῷ Θεῷ παρα δεξώμεθα ὡς δόκιμοι τραπεζῖται, τὰ δὲ ἀδόκιμα καὶ
δυσάρεστα αὐτῷ ἀποσειώ μεθα. ἐπεὶ δὲ ἀπήρτηται τὰ τῆς φράσεως, δοκεῖ μοι οὕτως
ἂν ἀποκαταστῆναι, μὴ οὖν γίνεσθε συμμέτοχοι αὐτῶν, δοκιμάζοντες τί ἐστὶν
εὐάρεστον τῷ Κυρίῳ. εἰ καὶ ἦτέ ποτε σκότος, νῦν δὲ φῶς ὄντες ἐν Κυρίῳ ὡς τέκνα
φωτὸς περιπατεῖτε, τοὺς καρποὺς ἐπιδεικνύμενοι τοῦ φωτὸς ἐν πάσῃ ἀγαθωσύνῃ καὶ
δικαιοσύνῃ καὶ ἀληθείᾳ. [v 11a] καὶ μὴ συγκοινωνεῖτε τοῖς ἔργοις τοῖς ἀκάρποις τοῦ
σκότους. καὶ ἐν ἄλλοις τὸ μὲν τοῦ καρποῦ ὄνομα ἔταξεν ἐπὶ τοῦ πνεύματος τὸ δὲ τοῦ
ἔργου ἐπὶ τῆς σαρκός, εἰπὼν φανερὰ δέ ἐ τι τὰ ἔργα τῆ αρκό , ἅτινά ἐ τι πορνεία καὶ
τὰ ἑξῆς, ὁ δὲ καρπὸ τοῦ πνεύματό ἐ τιν ἀγάπη χαρὰ εἰρήνη καὶ τὰ ἑξῆς. νῦν
μέντοιγε τὰ τοῦ σκότους ἔργα ἄκαρπα εἶναί φησιν, οἷς κοινωνεῖ ὁ ποιῶν αὐτά. [v
11b] μᾶλλον δὲ καὶ ἐλέγχετε. ἐν ταῖς ἐντολαῖς εἶναι νομιστέον καὶ τὸ ἐλέγχειν· ὅπερ
ποιήσει ὁ μὴ ἀκουσόμενος ἄν, ὑποκριτὰ ἔκβαλε πρῶτον ἐκ τοῦ ὀφθαλμοῦ ου τὴν
δοκὸν καὶ τότε διαβλέψει ἐκβαλεῖν τὸ κάρφο ἐκ τοῦ ὀφθαλμοῦ τοῦ ἀδελφοῦ ου.
διόπερ καὶ οἱ προφῆται, μηδαμῶς ἐλέγχοις ὑπεύθυνοι τυγχάνοντες, ἤλεγχον τοὺς
ἁμαρτάνοντας. [v 12] τὰ γὰρ κρυφῆ γινόμενα ὑπ' αὐτῶν αἰσχρόν ἐστι καὶ λέγειν.
τίνων αὐτῶν; οὐ πάνυ σαφῶς προεῖπεν· εἰ μὴ ἄρα τις ἀναφέρῃ ἐπὶ τοὺς υἱοὺς τῆς
ἀπειθείας τὴν λέξιν, ὥστε οὕτως αὐτὴν ἔχειν τὰ γὰρ κρυφῆ γινόμενα ὑπὸ τῶν υἱῶν
τῆς ἀπειθείας αἰσχρόν ἐστι καὶ λέγειν, ἅτινα ἦν πορνεία καὶ ἀκαθαρσία. 26 Eph. v13
[τὰ δὲ πάντα ἐλεγχόμενα ὑπὸ τοῦ φωτὸς φανεροῦνται· πᾶν γὰρ τὸ φανερούμενον
φῶς ἐστιν. διὸ λέγει, Ἔγειρε ὁ καθεύδων καὶ ἀνάστα ἐκ τῶν νεκρῶν, καὶ ἐπιφαύσει
σοι ὁ χριστός.] [Ὠριγένης δέ φησιν] ἐπείπερ τὰ ἐλεγχόμενα ἔργα τοῦ σκότους ὑπὸ
τοῦ φωτὸς φανεροῦται, μεταβαλλόντων τῶν ἐλεγχομένων εἰς φῶς, λέγεται τοῖς
καθεύδουσι καὶ ἐν νεκρότητι τυγχάνουσιν ἐκ τοῦ τὰ ἄκαρπα ἔργα τοῦ σκότους
πεποιηκέναι τὸ ἔγειρε ὁ καθεύδων καὶ ἀνάστα ἐκ τῶν νεκρῶν καὶ ἐπιφαύσει σοι ἁ
χριστός. ζητήσαι δ' ἄν τις, τίς λέγει κατὰ τὸ ἐνθάδε γεγραμμένον διὸ λέγει Ἔγειρε ὁ
καθεύδων καὶ ἀνάστα ἐκ τῶν νεκρῶν. ὁ μὲν οὖν τις φήσει ἔν τινι τῶν προφητῶν
ἀνεγνωκότα ταῦτα τὸν ἀπόστολον ἐνθάδε αὐτὸν ἀναγεγραφέναι. ἕτερος δὲ αὐτὸν
τὸν ἀπόστολον προσωποποιεῖν τινα ἐκ τοῦ πνεύματος λεγόμενα εἰς προτροπὴν τὴν
ἐπὶ μετάνοιαν. ἔτι δὲ ζητήσεις, πῶς τῷ αὐτῷ λέγεται ὡς μὲν ζῶντι καὶ καθεύδοντι
ἔγειρε ὁ καθεύδων, ὡς δὲ τεθνηκότι τὸ ἀνάστα ἐκ τῶν νεκρῶν. μήποτ' οὖν ἐπείπερ
ἔστι καὶ πνεῦμα τοῦ ἀνθρώπου τὸ ἐν αὐτῷ, ὅπερ ἐπὶ κρείττονος τετηρήκαμεν
λέγεσθαι, ἔστι δέ τι καὶ δεύτερον ἡ ψυχὴ τὸ καὶ νόσου καὶ θανάτου ἐκ τῶν
ἁμαρτημάτων δεκτικόν, τὸ μὲν ἔγειρε ὁ καθεύδων λέγεται διὰ τὸ πνεῦμα, τὸ δὲ
ἀνάστα ἐκ τῶν νεκρῶν διὰ τὴν ψυχήν· ἐπείπερ ψυχὴ ἡ ἁμαρτάνου α αὕτη
ἀποθανεῖται, τοῦ δὲ πνεύματος οὐδαμοῦ εὕρομεν θάνατον. φῶ δὲ ὢν ἀληθινὸν ὁ
χριστός ἐπιφαύσει τῷ ἐγειρομένῳ ἀπὸ ὕπνου καὶ ἀναστάντι ἐκ νεκρῶν. 27 Eph. v15–
17 βλέπετε οὖν ἀκριβῶς πῶς περιπατεῖτε, μὴ ὡς ἄσοφοι ἀλλ' ὡς σοφοί,
ἐξαγοραζόμενοι τὸν καιρὸν ὅτι αἱ ἡμέραι πονηραί εἰσιν. διὰ τοῦτο μὴ γίνεσθε
ἄφρονες, ἀλλὰ συνιέντες τί τὸ θέλημα τοῦ Κυρίου. [Ὠριγένης φησίν] ὁ δοκιμάζων
καθ' ἕκαστον ὧν λέγει καὶ πράττει καὶ ἐννοεῖ τὸ εὐάρεστον τῷ Κυρίῳ, δυνήσεται καὶ
βλέπειν ἀκριβῶς ἐκ τῆς πολλῆς προσοχῆς πῶς περιπατήσει, ὁ δὲ βλέπων ἀκριβῶς
πῶς περιπατήσει πάντως ἐστὶ σοφός. καὶ ἐπεὶ πρόθεσίν τινες ἔχουσι χρηστοτέραν, οὐ
σοφοὶ δὲ τυγχάνοντες θέλουσι βλέπειν ἀκριβῶς πῶς περιπατοῦσι, προσέθηκε τὸ μὴ
ὡς ἄσοφοι ἀλλ' ὡς σοφοί· σοφίας δὲ ἔργον τὸ βλέπειν ἀκριβῶς καὶ τὰ ἠθικά.
ἐξαγοραζόμενοι τὸν καιρὸν ὅτι αἱ ἡμέραι πονηραί εἰσιν. οἱονεὶ ἑαυτοῖς τὸν καιρὸν
ὠνούμενοι, ἔχοντα ὡς πρὸς τὸν ἀνθρώπινον βίον πονηρὰς ἡμέρας. ὅτε οὖν εἴς τι
δέον τὸν καιρὸν καταναλίσκομεν, ὠνησάμεθα αὐτὸν καὶ ἀντηγοράσαμεν ἑαυτοῖς
ὡσπερεὶ πεπραμένον τῇ τῶν ἀνθρώπων κακίᾳ· οὐδεὶς δὲ βιωτικώτερον ζῶν καὶ ἐν
φροντίσιν ἢ μερίμναις τυγχάνων ἐώνηται ἑαυτῷ τὸν καιρόν, ἀλλ' ὁ μόνος εἴς τι
pass_a_gloss: And you will make them stop and consider also from Christ being justice. Now in the beneficent the goodness is shown, in the distributing according to worth the justice, and in the knowing of the reason of the whole the truth. Eph 5:10: testing what is well pleasing to the Lord. There is need of doing all things with counsel, so that, examining around each of the things to be done from examination, we may receive the approved things and the things well pleasing to God as approved bankers, and the unapproved things and those ill pleasing to him we may shake off. And since the parts of the phrase have been detached, it seems to me it might be restored this way: do not then become co-partakers of them, testing what is well pleasing to the Lord. If you were also once darkness, but now being light in the Lord walk as children of light, displaying the fruits of the light in all goodness and justice and truth. Eph 5:11a: and do not have fellowship with the unfruitful works of the darkness. Also in other places he set the name of the fruit upon the Spirit and that of the work upon the flesh, having said "and the works of the flesh are manifest, which are fornication" and the next things, "but the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace" and the next things. Now however he says the works of the darkness are unfruitful, with which the one doing them shares. Eph 5:11b: but rather also convict them. One must hold that the convicting also is among the commandments; which the one who would not hear "hypocrite, cast out first from your eye the beam and then you will see through to cast out the mote from the eye of your brother" will do. Wherefore also the prophets, being in no way liable to convictions, convicted the sinners. Eph 5:12: for the things happening secretly by them it is shameful even to say. Of whom, them? He did not foretell quite clearly; unless then someone refers the phrase to the sons of disobedience, so that it holds thus: for the things happening secretly by the sons of disobedience it is shameful even to say, which were fornication and uncleanness. Eph 5:13-14 lemma: but all things being convicted by the light are manifested; for everything being manifested is light. Wherefore he says, Rise up, the sleeping one, and stand up out of the dead, and the Christ will shine upon you. [Origen says] since the convicted works of the darkness are manifested by the light, the convicted things changing into light, there is said to those sleeping and being in deadness from having done the unfruitful works of the darkness the "rise up, sleeper, and stand up from the dead and the Christ will shine on you". And someone might seek who says, according to what is written here, "wherefore he says, rise up sleeper and stand up from the dead". One person will say that the apostle, having read these things in one of the prophets, wrote them down here; another that the apostle himself personifies certain things spoken from the Spirit for exhortation to repentance. And still you will seek how to the same one it is said, as to one living and sleeping, "rise up, sleeper", but as to one having died, "stand up from the dead". Perhaps then, since there is also a spirit of the human being, the one in him, which we have observed said of the better, and there is also some second thing, the soul, receptive of both disease and death from the sins, the "rise up sleeper" is said on account of the spirit, and the "stand up from the dead" on account of the soul; since the soul that sins, this will die, but of the spirit we found death nowhere. And Christ, being true light, will shine upon the one raised from sleep and having stood up from the dead. Eph 5:15-17 lemma: see then precisely how you walk, not as unwise but as wise, buying out the season because the days are wicked. On account of this do not become senseless, but understanding what the will of the Lord is. [Origen says] The one testing in each of the things he says and does and thinks the thing well pleasing to the Lord will be able also to see precisely, from much attention, how he will walk; and the one seeing precisely how he will walk is altogether wise. And since some have a kinder purpose, but not being wise want to see precisely how they walk, he added the "not as unwise but as wise"; and the work of wisdom is seeing precisely also the moral things. Buying out the season because the days are wicked: as it were purchasing for themselves the season, which has, as regards human life, wicked days. So when we spend the season on something needed, we purchased it and bought it in exchange for ourselves as if sold to the wickedness of men; and no one living more for livelihood and being in concerns or cares has purchased for himself the season, but only the one who, on something ...
pass_b_english: You will also bring them up short with the fact that Christ is justice. Goodness shows itself in doing good; justice in giving each what he deserves; and truth in knowing the reason of all things.

"Testing what is pleasing to the Lord" (Ephesians 5:10). We need to do everything with deliberation, so that, looking closely at each thing to be done and examining it, we may accept, like approved money changers, what passes the test and pleases God, and shake off what fails the test and displeases him. Since the phrasing is left hanging, it seems to me it could be restored like this: "Do not, then, become fellow partakers with them, testing what is pleasing to the Lord. Even if you were once darkness, now, being light in the Lord, walk as children of light, showing the fruits of the light in all goodness and justice and truth."

"And take no part in the fruitless works of darkness" (Ephesians 5:11). Elsewhere too he gave the name "fruit" to what belongs to the Spirit and "work" to what belongs to the flesh, when he said, "Now the works of the flesh are plain: they are fornication" and the rest, "but the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace" and the rest (Galatians 5:19-22). Here, though, he says that the works of darkness are fruitless, and the one who does them takes part in them.

"But rather expose them" (Ephesians 5:11). Exposing, too, must be counted among the commandments. It will be done by the one who would not hear, "Hypocrite, first take the beam out of your own eye, and then you will see clearly to take the speck out of your brother's eye" (Matthew 7:5). That is why the prophets, who were in no way open to reproof themselves, reproved those who sinned.

"For the things done by them in secret are shameful even to speak of" (Ephesians 5:12). By whom? He has not said quite clearly beforehand, unless one refers the phrase to the sons of disobedience, so that it reads: "For the things done in secret by the sons of disobedience are shameful even to speak of." And those things were fornication and uncleanness.

"But all things, when they are exposed by the light, are made plain; for everything that is made plain is light. Therefore it says, 'Awake, sleeper, and rise from the dead, and Christ will shine on you'" (Ephesians 5:13-14). Origen says: Since the works of darkness, once exposed, are made plain by the light, as the things exposed are changed into light, it is said to those who are asleep and lie in deadness because they have done the fruitless works of darkness, "Awake, sleeper, and rise from the dead, and Christ will shine on you."

Someone might ask who it is that speaks in what is written here, "Therefore it says, Awake, sleeper, and rise from the dead." One will say that the apostle read these words in one of the prophets and wrote them down here. Another will say that the apostle himself is giving a voice to words spoken by the Spirit, to urge people toward repentance.

You will ask, further, how the same person is told "Awake, sleeper," as one who is alive and asleep, and "Rise from the dead," as one who has died. Perhaps, then, it is this: there is the spirit of the man that is in him, which we have observed is spoken of as the better part; and there is something second, the soul, which can receive both sickness and death from sins. So "Awake, sleeper" is said because of the spirit, and "Rise from the dead" because of the soul; for "the soul that sins, it shall die" (Ezekiel 18:4), but nowhere have we found a death of the spirit. And Christ, being the true light, will shine on the one who is roused from sleep and has risen from the dead.

"See, then, that you walk carefully, not as unwise but as wise, redeeming the time, because the days are evil. Therefore do not become foolish, but understand what the will of the Lord is" (Ephesians 5:15-17). Origen says: Whoever tests, in each thing he says and does and thinks, what is pleasing to the Lord will also be able, from close attention, to see carefully how he is to walk; and whoever sees carefully how he is to walk is wise in every way. And since some have a fairly good intention, yet, not being wise, want to see carefully how they walk, he added, "not as unwise but as wise." For to see carefully, even in matters of conduct, is the work of wisdom.

"Redeeming the time, because the days are evil." As if buying the time for yourselves, time that holds evil days as far as human life goes. When we spend the time on something needful, then, we have bought it and bought it back for ourselves, as though it had been sold to human wickedness. No one who lives too much for this life, caught up in cares or anxieties, has bought the time for himself; only the one who spends it on something

choices.english: You will also bring them up short
choices.why: ἐφίστημι with a personal object: make the opponents stop and attend; continues the argument against those who split the just God from the good.
'Expose' in the lemma (light imagery); 'reprove' where the prophets reprove sinners, as the Greek turns to moral rebuke.

choices.english: only the one who spends it on something
choices.why: The section breaks inside the clause; the participle ἀναλίσκων αὐτόν stands at the start of u06-rem-mid. English order needs the verb here; u06-rem-mid begins with the rest of the clause ('needful...').

choices.english: lives too much for this life
choices.why: Comparative of βιωτικός: absorbed in ordinary livelihood.
